## Commit style

Imperative subject under 72 characters. Explain *why* in the body when the reason
is not obvious from the diff. This codebase has several fixes whose rationale is
impossible to guess — keep documenting them.

# Free and near-free options, compared

Every provider advertises a free tier. For a VPN, the number that matters is not CPU or RAM —
WireGuard needs almost none of either — it is **egress**. Most free tiers are generous with
compute and stingy with bandwidth, which is exactly backwards for this workload.

*Figures current as of September 2026. Cloud pricing changes; verify before relying on it.*

---

## Summary

| Provider | Sign up | Cost | Egress/month | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Oracle Cloud Always Free** | [oracle.com/cloud/free](https://www.oracle.com/cloud/free/) | $0 forever | **10 TB** | Best free option by a distance — if you can get capacity |
| **Azure free account** | [azure.microsoft.com/free](https://azure.microsoft.com/free/) | $0 for 12 months | 100 GB | One region, one always-on VM, then it expires |
| **AWS Lightsail** | [aws.amazon.com/lightsail/pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/lightsail/pricing/) | $3.50-$5/mo | 0.5-1 TB | Not free, but the cheapest thing that always works |
| **AWS Free Tier** | [aws.amazon.com/free](https://aws.amazon.com/free/) | $100-200 credits | — | Credit-based since July 2025; no 12-month EC2 tier |
| **Google Cloud Always Free** | [cloud.google.com/free](https://cloud.google.com/free) | $0 forever | **1 GB** | Unusable for a VPN |

---

## Oracle Cloud Always Free

The only genuinely free-forever option with enough bandwidth to matter: **10 TB of egress per
month**, roughly twenty times a $5 Lightsail bundle, on an Ampere A1 ARM instance.

The catches are real:

- Oracle **halved** the Always Free A1 allowance from 4 OCPU/24 GB to **2 OCPU/12 GB** effective
  15 June 2026, with no blog post or customer notification, and began terminating instances
  above the new limit from 18 August 2026.
- A1 capacity is frequently unavailable. `Out of host capacity` errors are common in US regions
  and can persist for hours or days. European and Asian regions provision more reliably.
- Free-tier instances can be reclaimed if idle.

Still 2 OCPU and 12 GB of RAM — vastly more than a VPN needs — for nothing. If you can
provision one, take it. Just do not make it the only way you can reach the internet.

Regions covering the common cases: `us-sanjose-1`, `us-phoenix-1`, `ap-mumbai-1`,
`ap-singapore-1`, `eu-frankfurt-1`.

---

## Azure free account

A new Azure account includes **750 hours/month of a B1s VM for 12 months**, which is exactly one
always-on server, plus $200 in credits valid for the first 30 days. Egress is free for the first
100 GB per month.

Good for a full year of one always-on region. Not useful for multi-region, since 750 hours is a
single VM's worth of uptime.

---

## AWS

**The 12-month free tier is gone for new accounts.** Since 15 July 2025, accounts created after
that date get a credit-based model instead: $100 on signup, growing to $200 by completing
onboarding tasks, on either a Free plan (closes after six months or when credits run out) or a
Paid plan. Accounts created *before* that date keep the old 12-month allowances.

So on a new AWS account, Lightsail is not free — but at $5/month flat with 1 TB of transfer, and
billed hourly so you can delete it when idle, it is the cheapest option that provisions reliably
every single time. That predictability is why this repository defaults to it.

Note that AWS's 100 GB/month free egress allowance is **account-wide**, not per region, and
applies to EC2 rather than to Lightsail bundles, which have their own included transfer.

---

## Google Cloud

The Always Free `e2-micro` in `us-west1`, `us-central1`, or `us-east1` includes **1 GB of
outbound transfer per month**. A single video call will exhaust it.

GCP is a paid option for this use case. The $300/90-day trial credit will cover a VPN
comfortably while it lasts.

---

## Recommendation

- **Want free and will tolerate flakiness** → Oracle Cloud Always Free.
- **Want it to work every time** → AWS Lightsail, `down` when idle, ~$0.42-1.67/month.
- **Have a new Azure account** → take the 12 free months for your home region, and use
  Lightsail on-demand for everywhere else.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# vpn.sh — spin a personal WireGuard server up and down, in any cloud region.
#
#   ./vpn.sh up aws us-west-2        launch a server and write client configs
#   ./vpn.sh down aws us-west-2      delete it and stop the billing
#
# Every key is generated locally and injected through cloud-init, so a region
# can be destroyed and recreated without any client config changing except the
# endpoint address. See README.md for the full command reference.

set -euo pipefail

# macOS still ships bash 3.2, so this tool stays 3.2-compatible: no associative
# arrays, no ${var,,}, no mapfile. Guard anyway so a truly ancient shell fails
# with a readable message instead of a syntax error.
if [ -z "${BASH_VERSINFO:-}" ] || [ "${BASH_VERSINFO[0]}" -lt 3 ]; then
  echo "vpn.sh needs bash 3.2 or newer. Run it with: bash ./vpn.sh ..." >&2
  exit 1
fi

ROOT_DIR="$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"

# shellcheck source=lib/common.sh
source "$ROOT_DIR/lib/common.sh"

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- defaults --

AWS_PROFILE="${AWS_PROFILE:-default}"
GCP_PROJECT="${GCP_PROJECT:-}"
AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION="${AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION:-}"
DNS_MODE="cloudflare"
SSH_CIDR=""
SSH_PUBLIC=0
IPV6_ONLY=0
CLIENTS=""

usage() {
  cat <<'EOF'
vpn.sh — your own WireGuard VPN, in any region, billed by the hour.

USAGE
  ./vpn.sh <command> [args] [flags]

COMMANDS
  up <provider> <region>       Launch a server; write client configs
  down <provider> <region>     Delete the server; billing stops immediately
  status                       Show every known server and whether it is live
  sync <provider> <region>     Push the current client list to a running server
  config <provider> <region> [client]   Print a client config to stdout
  qr <provider> <region> [client]       Print a scannable QR code
  client add <name>            Create a new client keypair
  client list                  List clients
  client rm <name>             Remove a client (run `sync` afterwards)
  regions <provider>           List regions the provider supports
  ssh <provider> <region>      Open a shell on the server (connect the VPN first)
  logs <provider> <region>     Show the server's bootstrap log and WireGuard state
  unlock <provider> <region>   Re-apply firewall rules (use with --ssh-public)
  doctor                       Check local prerequisites
  pool [n]                     Print your egress addresses as /32s for --ssh-cidr

PROVIDERS
  aws      Amazon Lightsail  (primary, fully supported)
  gcp      Google Compute Engine
  azure    Azure Virtual Machines

FLAGS
  --profile <name>     AWS CLI profile              (default: $AWS_PROFILE, or AWS_PROFILE)
  --project <id>       GCP project id               (or GCP_PROJECT)
  --subscription <id>  Azure subscription id        (or AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION)
  --clients a,b,c      Client names to create       (default: existing, else "laptop,phone")
  --dns <mode>         cloudflare | quad9 | google | unbound | adguard | <ip,ip>
                       Default is cloudflare (1.1.1.2 — malware-blocking, no logs)
  --ssh-public         Expose TCP 22 to the internet, restricted to --ssh-cidr.
                       Off by default: SSH is reachable over the tunnel instead,
                       so only one UDP port faces the internet.
  --ssh-cidr <list>    Used with --ssh-public. Comma-separated CIDRs; default is
                       your current IP as a /32. Behind CGNAT, run `./vpn.sh pool`
                       and pass the list rather than widening to a /24.
  --ipv6-only          Use the cheaper IPv6-only bundle. AWS only. See README caveat.
  --port <n>           UDP listen port              (default: 51820)
  -h, --help           This message

EXAMPLES
  ./vpn.sh up aws us-west-2 --profile myvpn --clients laptop,phone
  ./vpn.sh qr aws us-west-2 phone
  ./vpn.sh down aws us-west-2
EOF
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------ flag parsing --

POSITIONAL=()
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --profile)      AWS_PROFILE="${2:?--profile needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --project)      GCP_PROJECT="${2:?--project needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --subscription) AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION="${2:?--subscription needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --clients)      CLIENTS="${2:?--clients needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --dns)          DNS_MODE="${2:?--dns needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --ssh-cidr)     SSH_CIDR="${2:?--ssh-cidr needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --ssh-public)   SSH_PUBLIC=1; shift ;;
    --port)         VPN_PORT="${2:?--port needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --ipv6-only)    IPV6_ONLY=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)      usage; exit 0 ;;
    --)             shift; POSITIONAL+=("$@"); break ;;
    -*)             die "unknown flag: $1 (try --help)" ;;
    *)              POSITIONAL+=("$1"); shift ;;
  esac
done
set -- "${POSITIONAL[@]:-}"

[[ $# -eq 0 || -z "${1:-}" ]] && { usage; exit 1; }

# ------------------------------------------------------------- dispatching --

# Sourcing and credential-checking are separate: `status` wants the functions
# without aborting the whole run when one provider's CLI is absent.
source_provider() {
  # shellcheck source=/dev/null
  case "$1" in
    aws|gcp|azure) source "$ROOT_DIR/lib/provider-$1.sh" ;;
    *) die "unknown provider: $1 (expected aws, gcp, or azure)" ;;
  esac
}

load_provider() {
  # Exported so the provider libraries read the same values regardless of how
  # they are invoked; also tells shellcheck these are used elsewhere.
  export SSH_CIDR SSH_PUBLIC AWS_PROFILE GCP_PROJECT AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION
  source_provider "$1"
  "${1}_check"
}

require_region() {
  [[ -n "${1:-}" ]] || die "missing region. Try: ./vpn.sh regions $2"
}

# Create the server keypair and per-client preshared keys once, and keep them.
# Regenerating a region therefore produces an identical server public key, so
# previously issued client configs stay valid apart from the endpoint line.
server_ensure() {
  local prov="$1" region="$2" skey priv
  skey="$(server_key "$prov" "$region")"
  if [[ "$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"] // empty")" == "" ]]; then
    priv="$(wg_genkey)"
    state_set '.servers[$k] = {provider:$p, region:$r, priv:$priv, pub:$pub,
                               port:($port|tonumber), dns:$dns, psk:{}, created:$t}' \
      --arg k "$skey" --arg p "$prov" --arg r "$region" \
      --arg priv "$priv" --arg pub "$(wg_pubkey "$priv")" \
      --arg port "$VPN_PORT" --arg dns "$(resolve_dns "$DNS_MODE")" \
      --arg t "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
    ok "created server keypair for $skey"
  else
    # Keep the resolver and port in step with the flags given on this run.
    state_set '.servers[$k].dns = $dns | .servers[$k].port = ($port|tonumber)' \
      --arg k "$skey" --arg dns "$(resolve_dns "$DNS_MODE")" --arg port "$VPN_PORT"
  fi
  # A preshared key per client-server pair adds a symmetric layer on top of
  # the X25519 handshake. Cheap, and hedges against future cryptanalysis.
  while IFS= read -r c; do
    [[ -z "$c" ]] && continue
    if [[ "$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"].psk[\"$c\"] // empty")" == "" ]]; then
      state_set '.servers[$k].psk[$c] = $v' \
        --arg k "$skey" --arg c "$c" --arg v "$(wg_genpsk)"
    fi
  done < <(state_get '.clients | keys[]')
}

ensure_clients_exist() {
  local list="${CLIENTS:-}"
  if [[ -z "$list" ]]; then
    [[ "$(state_get '.clients | length')" -gt 0 ]] && return 0
    list="laptop,phone"
    log "no clients yet — creating defaults: $list"
  fi
  # Split on commas without setting IFS for the whole function: a modified IFS
  # leaks into every function called from here, which silently breaks word
  # splitting inside them.
  local c
  while IFS= read -r c; do
    c="$(echo "$c" | tr -d '[:space:]')"
    [[ -z "$c" ]] && continue
    [[ "$c" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ]] || die "invalid client name '$c' (use letters, digits, - and _)"
    client_ensure "$c"
  done < <(printf '%s\n' "$list" | tr ',' '\n')   # trailing newline: read drops an unterminated final field
}

cmd="$1"; shift || true
check_base_deps
state_init

case "$cmd" in

  up)
    prov="${1:?usage: ./vpn.sh up <provider> <region>}"; require_region "${2:-}" "$prov"; region="$2"
    load_provider "$prov"
    ensure_clients_exist
    server_ensure "$prov" "$region"
    case "$prov" in
      aws)   aws_up   "$region" "$DNS_MODE" "$IPV6_ONLY" ;;
      gcp)   gcp_up   "$region" "$DNS_MODE" ;;
      azure) azure_up "$region" "$DNS_MODE" ;;
    esac
    emit_configs "$prov" "$region"
    echo
    ok "server is booting. WireGuard usually answers 60-90s after launch."
    echo "  Import a config:  $CLIENT_DIR/$prov-$region/<client>.conf"
    echo "  Scan a QR code:   ./vpn.sh qr $prov $region phone"
    echo "  Stop paying:      ./vpn.sh down $prov $region"
    ;;

  down)
    prov="${1:?usage: ./vpn.sh down <provider> <region>}"; require_region "${2:-}" "$prov"; region="$2"
    load_provider "$prov"
    case "$prov" in
      aws)   aws_down   "$region" ;;
      gcp)   gcp_down   "$region" ;;
      azure) azure_down "$region" ;;
    esac
    ;;

  sync)
    prov="${1:?usage: ./vpn.sh sync <provider> <region>}"; require_region "${2:-}" "$prov"; region="$2"
    load_provider "$prov"
    server_ensure "$prov" "$region"
    skey="$(server_key "$prov" "$region")"
    log "pushing current peer list to $skey"
    peers=""
    while IFS= read -r name; do
      [[ -z "$name" ]] && continue
      peers+=$'\n'"# client: $name"$'\n'"[Peer]"$'\n'
      peers+="PublicKey = $(state_get ".clients[\"$name\"].pub")"$'\n'
      psk="$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"].psk[\"$name\"] // empty")"
      [[ -n "$psk" ]] && peers+="PresharedKey = $psk"$'\n'
      peers+="AllowedIPs = $(state_get ".clients[\"$name\"].ipv4")/32, $(state_get ".clients[\"$name\"].ipv6")/128"$'\n'
    done < <(state_get '.clients | keys[]')
    printf '%s\n' "$peers" | "${prov}_ssh" "$region" "sudo /usr/local/sbin/wg-setpeers"
    emit_configs "$prov" "$region"
    ok "peers synced and configs rewritten"
    ;;

  status)
    printf '%-22s %-16s %-10s %s\n' "SERVER" "ENDPOINT" "STATE" "DNS"
    while IFS= read -r skey; do
      [[ -z "$skey" ]] && continue
      p="${skey%%/*}"; r="${skey##*/}"
      ep="$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"].endpoint // \"-\"")"
      dns="$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"].dns")"
      st="unknown"
      source_provider "$p"
      # Run the credential check in a subshell: it calls die() on failure, and
      # die() exits, which would otherwise abort the whole status table.
      if ( "${p}_check" ) >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        st="$("${p}_state" "$r" 2>/dev/null || echo absent)"
      else
        st="no-creds"
      fi
      [[ "$st" == "running" ]] && st="${C_GRN}running${C_RST}"
      [[ "$st" == "absent"  ]] && st="${C_DIM}absent${C_RST}"
      printf '%-22s %-16s %-20b %s\n' "$skey" "$ep" "$st" "$dns"
    done < <(state_get '.servers | keys[]')
    echo
    echo "clients: $(state_get '.clients | keys | join(", ")')"
    ;;

  config)
    prov="${1:?usage: ./vpn.sh config <provider> <region> [client]}"
    require_region "${2:-}" "$prov"; region="$2"
    client="${3:-$(state_get '.clients | keys[0]')}"
    render_client_config "$client" "$prov" "$region"
    ;;

  qr)
    prov="${1:?usage: ./vpn.sh qr <provider> <region> [client]}"
    require_region "${2:-}" "$prov"; region="$2"
    client="${3:-$(state_get '.clients | keys[0]')}"
    [[ "$(state_get ".clients[\"$client\"] // empty")" != "" ]] || die "unknown client: $client"
    [[ "$(state_get ".servers[\"$prov/$region\"].endpoint // \"null\"")" != "null" ]] \
      || die "$prov/$region is not up. Run: ./vpn.sh up $prov $region"
    mkdir -p "$CLIENT_DIR/$prov-$region"; chmod 700 "$CLIENT_DIR/$prov-$region"
    f="$CLIENT_DIR/$prov-$region/$client.conf"
    render_client_config "$client" "$prov" "$region" > "$f.tmp"
    chmod 600 "$f.tmp"; mv "$f.tmp" "$f"
    echo "  $prov/$region — $client"
    show_qr "$f"
    ;;

  client)
    sub="${1:-list}"; shift || true
    case "$sub" in
      add)  client_ensure "${1:?usage: ./vpn.sh client add <name>}" ;;
      list) state_get '.clients | to_entries[] | "\(.key)\t\(.value.ipv4)"' | column -t ;;
      rm)   name="${1:?usage: ./vpn.sh client rm <name>}"
            state_set 'del(.clients[$n]) | .servers |= map_values(.psk |= del(.[$n]))' --arg n "$name"
            ok "removed client $name — run 'vpn.sh sync' on each live server" ;;
      *)    die "unknown client subcommand: $sub" ;;
    esac
    ;;

  logs)
    # The bootstrap script keeps a log on the server. This is the first thing to
    # look at when an instance is running but nothing answers on the VPN port.
    prov="${1:?usage: ./vpn.sh logs <provider> <region>}"
    require_region "${2:-}" "$prov"; region="$2"
    load_provider "$prov"
    "${prov}_ssh" "$region" \
      "sudo tail -60 /var/log/vpn-bootstrap.log 2>/dev/null || echo '(no bootstrap log — the script never started)';
       echo; echo '--- wg ---'; sudo wg show 2>&1 | head -20;
       echo '--- markers ---'; ls -l /var/lib/wg-ready /var/lib/wg-failed 2>&1;
       echo '--- failure detail ---'; sudo cat /var/lib/wg-failed 2>/dev/null | tail -20"
    ;;

  unlock)
    prov="${1:?usage: ./vpn.sh unlock <provider> <region>}"
    require_region "${2:-}" "$prov"; region="$2"
    load_provider "$prov"
    # Home ISPs hand out a new address regularly, which locks you out of SSH
    # because the allow-rule still names the old one. Re-pin it.
    "${prov}_open_ports" "$region"
    ok "SSH re-pinned to your current address"
    ;;

  regions)
    prov="${1:?usage: ./vpn.sh regions <provider>}"
    load_provider "$prov"
    "${prov}_regions"
    ;;

  ssh)
    prov="${1:?usage: ./vpn.sh ssh <provider> <region>}"
    require_region "${2:-}" "$prov"; region="$2"; shift 2
    load_provider "$prov"
    "${prov}_ssh" "$region" "$@"
    ;;

  pool)
    # Print the set of addresses this machine exits from, ready to paste into
    # --ssh-cidr. Useful when your ISP rotates you between several.
    log "sampling egress addresses (this takes a few seconds)"
    egress_pool "${1:-40}"
    ;;

  doctor)
    log "checking local prerequisites"
    ok "openssl $(openssl version | awk '{print $2}') — X25519 available"
    ok "jq $(jq --version)"
    command -v aws       >/dev/null && ok "aws $(aws --version 2>&1 | awk '{print $1}')" || warn "aws CLI not found (needed for --provider aws)"
    command -v gcloud    >/dev/null && ok "gcloud present" || warn "gcloud not found (needed for gcp)"
    command -v az        >/dev/null && ok "az present"     || warn "az not found (needed for azure)"
    command -v qrencode  >/dev/null && ok "qrencode present" || warn "qrencode not found — QR codes unavailable (brew install qrencode)"
    ;;

  -h|--help|help) usage ;;
  *) die "unknown command: $cmd (try --help)" ;;
esac

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# provider-gcp.sh — Google Compute Engine backend.
#
# Note on cost: GCP's Always Free e2-micro includes only 1 GB of egress per
# month, which is far too little for a VPN. Treat GCE as a paid option; the
# cheapest practical shape is an e2-micro on a Spot/preemptible-free tier in
# us-west1/us-central1/us-east1 plus metered egress at ~$0.085-0.12/GB.

GCP_MACHINE="${GCP_MACHINE:-e2-micro}"
GCP_IMAGE_FAMILY="${GCP_IMAGE_FAMILY:-ubuntu-2404-lts-amd64}"
GCP_IMAGE_PROJECT="${GCP_IMAGE_PROJECT:-ubuntu-os-cloud}"
GCP_FIREWALL="vpn-wireguard-allow"

gcp_check() {
  need_cmd gcloud "Install it: https://cloud.google.com/sdk/docs/install"
  [[ -n "$GCP_PROJECT" ]] || GCP_PROJECT="$(gcloud config get-value project 2>/dev/null)"
  [[ -n "$GCP_PROJECT" && "$GCP_PROJECT" != "(unset)" ]] \
    || die "no GCP project set. Pass --project <id> or run: gcloud config set project <id>"
  gcloud auth list --filter=status:ACTIVE --format='value(account)' 2>/dev/null | grep -q . \
    || die "not logged in to gcloud. Run: gcloud auth login"
}

gcp_instance_name() { echo "vpn-$1"; }
gcp_zone() { echo "$1-a"; }   # every GCE region has an -a zone

gcp_() { gcloud --project "$GCP_PROJECT" "$@"; }

gcp_regions() {
  gcp_ compute regions list --format='value(name,description)' 2>/dev/null
}

gcp_state() {
  local s
  s="$(gcp_ compute instances describe "$(gcp_instance_name "$1")" \
        --zone "$(gcp_zone "$1")" --format='value(status)' 2>/dev/null)" || { echo absent; return; }
  [[ "$s" == "RUNNING" ]] && echo running || echo "$s" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'
}

gcp_public_ip() {
  gcp_ compute instances describe "$(gcp_instance_name "$1")" --zone "$(gcp_zone "$1")" \
    --format='value(networkInterfaces[0].accessConfigs[0].natIP)' 2>/dev/null
}

# One project-wide firewall rule, scoped by target tag, rather than one per region.
gcp_open_ports() { gcp_ensure_firewall; }

gcp_ensure_firewall() {
  if gcp_ compute firewall-rules describe "$GCP_FIREWALL" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    gcp_ compute firewall-rules update "$GCP_FIREWALL" \
      --allow "udp:$VPN_PORT" --source-ranges 0.0.0.0/0 >/dev/null
  else
    step "creating firewall rule $GCP_FIREWALL (UDP $VPN_PORT from anywhere)"
    gcp_ compute firewall-rules create "$GCP_FIREWALL" \
      --allow "udp:$VPN_PORT" --source-ranges 0.0.0.0/0 \
      --target-tags wireguard-vpn --description "WireGuard VPN (managed by vpn.sh)" >/dev/null
  fi
  # SSH is restricted to the operator's current address.
  local cidr; cidr="$(ssh_cidr)"
  if gcp_ compute firewall-rules describe "${GCP_FIREWALL}-ssh" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    gcp_ compute firewall-rules update "${GCP_FIREWALL}-ssh" \
      --allow tcp:22 --source-ranges "$cidr" >/dev/null
  else
    gcp_ compute firewall-rules create "${GCP_FIREWALL}-ssh" \
      --allow tcp:22 --source-ranges "$cidr" --target-tags wireguard-vpn >/dev/null
  fi
}

gcp_up() {
  local region="$1" dns_mode="$2" name zone ip
  name="$(gcp_instance_name "$region")"; zone="$(gcp_zone "$region")"
  gcp_ensure_firewall

  if [[ "$(gcp_state "$region")" != "absent" ]]; then
    warn "instance $name already exists in $zone"
  else
    local ud; ud="$(mktemp)"
    build_user_data gcp "$region" "$dns_mode" > "$ud"
    log "launching $name in $zone ($GCP_MACHINE)"
    # can-ip-forward is mandatory: without it GCE drops forwarded packets.
    gcp_ compute instances create "$name" \
      --zone "$zone" \
      --machine-type "$GCP_MACHINE" \
      --image-family "$GCP_IMAGE_FAMILY" \
      --image-project "$GCP_IMAGE_PROJECT" \
      --boot-disk-size 10GB --boot-disk-type pd-standard \
      --can-ip-forward \
      --tags wireguard-vpn \
      --metadata-from-file "startup-script=$ud" \
      --labels "project=create-your-own-vpn,managed-by=vpn-sh" \
      >/dev/null || { rm -f "$ud"; die "instance creation failed in $zone"; }
    rm -f "$ud"
  fi

  log "waiting for instance to boot"
  local tries=0
  until [[ "$(gcp_state "$region")" == "running" ]]; do
    (( ++tries > 60 )) && { wait_end; die "instance did not reach RUNNING within 5 minutes"; }
    wait_dot; sleep 5
  done
  wait_end

  ip="$(gcp_public_ip "$region")"
  [[ -n "$ip" ]] || die "instance has no external IP"
  state_set '.servers[$k].endpoint = $e | .servers[$k].instance = $n | .servers[$k].updated = $t' \
    --arg k "$(server_key gcp "$region")" --arg e "$ip" --arg n "$name" --arg t "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  ok "$region is up at $ip"
}

gcp_down() {
  local region="$1" name zone
  name="$(gcp_instance_name "$region")"; zone="$(gcp_zone "$region")"
  if [[ "$(gcp_state "$region")" == "absent" ]]; then
    warn "no instance in $region — nothing to delete"; return 0
  fi
  log "deleting $name in $zone"
  gcp_ compute instances delete "$name" --zone "$zone" --quiet >/dev/null \
    || die "instance deletion failed"
  state_set '.servers[$k].endpoint = null | .servers[$k].instance = null | .servers[$k].updated = $t' \
    --arg k "$(server_key gcp "$region")" --arg t "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  ok "$region deleted — billing for it has stopped"
}

gcp_ssh() {
  local region="$1"; shift
  gcp_ compute ssh "$(gcp_instance_name "$region")" --zone "$(gcp_zone "$region")" \
    --tunnel-through-iap=false --command "$*"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# provider-azure.sh — Azure Virtual Machines backend.
#
# Cost note: Azure bills the VM, the managed disk, and the public IP address
# separately, so the all-in monthly figure lands well above an equivalent
# Lightsail bundle. Azure is worth it mainly for the 12-month free B1s
# allowance on a new account (750 h/month — enough for one always-on server).

AZ_SIZE="${AZ_SIZE:-Standard_B1ls}"
AZ_IMAGE="${AZ_IMAGE:-Canonical:ubuntu-24_04-lts:server:latest}"
AZ_ADMIN="${AZ_ADMIN:-azureuser}"

azure_check() {
  need_cmd az "Install it: https://learn.microsoft.com/cli/azure/install-azure-cli"
  az account show >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "not logged in to Azure. Run: az login"
  if [[ -n "$AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION" ]]; then
    az account set --subscription "$AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION" \
      || die "could not select subscription $AZURE_SUBSCRIPTION"
  fi
}

azure_rg()   { echo "vpn-$1-rg"; }
azure_name() { echo "vpn-$1"; }

azure_regions() {
  az account list-locations --query '[].[name,displayName]' --output tsv 2>/dev/null
}

azure_state() {
  local s
  s="$(az vm get-instance-view --resource-group "$(azure_rg "$1")" --name "$(azure_name "$1")" \
       --query "instanceView.statuses[?starts_with(code,'PowerState/')].displayStatus | [0]" \
       --output tsv 2>/dev/null)" || { echo absent; return; }
  [[ -z "$s" ]] && { echo absent; return; }
  [[ "$s" == "VM running" ]] && echo running || echo "$s" | tr '[:upper:]' '[:lower:]'
}

azure_public_ip() {
  az vm list-ip-addresses --resource-group "$(azure_rg "$1")" --name "$(azure_name "$1")" \
    --query '[0].virtualMachine.network.publicIpAddresses[0].ipAddress' --output tsv 2>/dev/null
}

# Re-apply the NSG rules, including pinning SSH to the caller's current address.
azure_open_ports() {
  local region="$1" rg name cidr
  rg="$(azure_rg "$region")"; name="$(azure_name "$region")"; cidr="$(ssh_cidr)"
  az network nsg rule update --resource-group "$rg" --nsg-name "${name}NSG" \
    --name allow-ssh --source-address-prefixes "$cidr" >/dev/null \
    || die "could not update NSG rule allow-ssh in $rg"
  step "SSH restricted to $cidr"
}

azure_up() {
  local region="$1" dns_mode="$2" rg name ip cidr
  rg="$(azure_rg "$region")"; name="$(azure_name "$region")"

  if [[ "$(azure_state "$region")" != "absent" ]]; then
    warn "VM $name already exists in $region"
  else
    step "ensuring resource group $rg"
    az group create --name "$rg" --location "$region" \
      --tags project=create-your-own-vpn managed-by=vpn.sh >/dev/null \
      || die "could not create resource group $rg"

    local ud; ud="$(mktemp)"
    build_user_data azure "$region" "$dns_mode" > "$ud"

    log "launching $name in $region ($AZ_SIZE)"
    # --generate-ssh-keys reuses ~/.ssh/id_rsa if present, otherwise creates it.
    az vm create \
      --resource-group "$rg" --name "$name" \
      --image "$AZ_IMAGE" --size "$AZ_SIZE" \
      --admin-username "$AZ_ADMIN" --generate-ssh-keys \
      --public-ip-sku Standard --public-ip-address-allocation static \
      --os-disk-size-gb 30 --storage-sku StandardSSD_LRS \
      --custom-data "$ud" \
      --nsg-rule NONE \
      --tags project=create-your-own-vpn managed-by=vpn.sh \
      >/dev/null || { rm -f "$ud"; die "vm create failed in $region"; }
    rm -f "$ud"

    # Azure does not forward packets for a NIC unless IP forwarding is enabled
    # on the NIC resource itself, independent of the in-guest sysctl.
    local nic
    nic="$(az vm show --resource-group "$rg" --name "$name" \
           --query 'networkProfile.networkInterfaces[0].id' --output tsv)"
    az network nic update --ids "$nic" --ip-forwarding true >/dev/null
  fi

  cidr="$(ssh_cidr)"
  step "opening UDP $VPN_PORT to the internet, SSH to $cidr"
  az network nsg rule create --resource-group "$rg" --nsg-name "${name}NSG" \
    --name allow-wireguard --priority 1000 --protocol Udp \
    --destination-port-ranges "$VPN_PORT" --source-address-prefixes '*' \
    --access Allow --direction Inbound >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
  az network nsg rule update --resource-group "$rg" --nsg-name "${name}NSG" \
    --name allow-wireguard --destination-port-ranges "$VPN_PORT" >/dev/null
  az network nsg rule create --resource-group "$rg" --nsg-name "${name}NSG" \
    --name allow-ssh --priority 1001 --protocol Tcp \
    --destination-port-ranges 22 --source-address-prefixes "$cidr" \
    --access Allow --direction Inbound >/dev/null 2>&1 || \
  az network nsg rule update --resource-group "$rg" --nsg-name "${name}NSG" \
    --name allow-ssh --source-address-prefixes "$cidr" >/dev/null

  log "waiting for VM to boot"
  local tries=0
  until [[ "$(azure_state "$region")" == "running" ]]; do
    (( ++tries > 60 )) && { wait_end; die "VM did not reach running within 5 minutes"; }
    wait_dot; sleep 5
  done
  wait_end

  ip="$(azure_public_ip "$region")"
  [[ -n "$ip" ]] || die "VM has no public IP"
  state_set '.servers[$k].endpoint = $e | .servers[$k].instance = $n | .servers[$k].updated = $t' \
    --arg k "$(server_key azure "$region")" --arg e "$ip" --arg n "$name" --arg t "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  ok "$region is up at $ip"
}

azure_down() {
  local region="$1" rg
  rg="$(azure_rg "$region")"
  if ! az group show --name "$rg" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    warn "no resource group $rg — nothing to delete"; return 0
  fi
  log "deleting resource group $rg (VM, disk, NIC, public IP, NSG)"
  az group delete --name "$rg" --yes --no-wait \
    || die "resource group deletion failed"
  state_set '.servers[$k].endpoint = null | .servers[$k].instance = null | .servers[$k].updated = $t' \
    --arg k "$(server_key azure "$region")" --arg t "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  ok "$region deletion started — billing stops as resources are removed"
}

azure_ssh() {
  local region="$1"; shift
  local ip; ip="$(azure_public_ip "$region")"
  [[ -n "$ip" ]] || die "no public IP for $region"
  ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
      -o LogLevel=ERROR "$AZ_ADMIN@$ip" "$@"
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# provider-aws.sh — Amazon Lightsail backend.
#
# Lightsail is used instead of EC2 because a personal VPN is an egress-heavy,
# tiny-compute workload. A $5 Lightsail bundle includes a public IPv4 address
# and 1 TB of transfer; the equivalent EC2 t3.micro costs ~$11.90/mo once the
# hourly public-IPv4 charge and EBS volume are counted, and bills egress from
# the first GB past the 100 GB account-wide free allowance.

AWS_BUNDLE_IPV4="${AWS_BUNDLE_IPV4:-nano_3_0}"
AWS_BUNDLE_IPV6="${AWS_BUNDLE_IPV6:-nano_ipv6_3_0}"
AWS_BLUEPRINT="${AWS_BLUEPRINT:-ubuntu_24_04}"

aws_() { aws --profile "$AWS_PROFILE" --region "$1" "${@:2}"; }

aws_check() {
  need_cmd aws "Install it: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/getting-started-install.html"
  aws sts get-caller-identity --profile "$AWS_PROFILE" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
    || die "AWS profile '$AWS_PROFILE' is not usable. Run: aws configure --profile $AWS_PROFILE"
}

aws_instance_name() { echo "vpn-$1"; }

aws_regions() {
  aws lightsail get-regions --profile "$AWS_PROFILE" --region us-east-1 \
    --query 'regions[].[name,displayName]' --output text
}

# Bundle availability differs per region: Lightsail suffixes the bundle id
# (_3_0 in most regions, _3_1 where the transfer allowance is halved), so the
# id is resolved against the live API rather than hardcoded.
aws_resolve_bundle() {
  local region="$1" want="$2" family id
  family="$(echo "$want" | sed 's/_[0-9]*_[0-9]*$//')"
  id="$(aws_ "$region" lightsail get-bundles \
    --query "bundles[?isActive && starts_with(bundleId, \`${family}_\`) && supportedPlatforms[0]=='LINUX_UNIX'].bundleId | [0]" \
    --output text 2>/dev/null)"
  [[ -n "$id" && "$id" != "None" ]] || die "no '$family' bundle available in $region"
  echo "$id"
}

aws_exists() {
  aws_ "$1" lightsail get-instance --instance-name "$(aws_instance_name "$1")" \
    >/dev/null 2>&1
}

aws_state() {
  aws_ "$1" lightsail get-instance --instance-name "$(aws_instance_name "$1")" \
    --query 'instance.state.name' --output text 2>/dev/null || echo "absent"
}

aws_public_ip() {
  aws_ "$1" lightsail get-instance --instance-name "$(aws_instance_name "$1")" \
    --query 'instance.publicIpAddress' --output text 2>/dev/null
}

# Only the VPN port is exposed. SSH is deliberately NOT opened to the internet:
# it is reachable over the tunnel at the server's VPN address instead, so the
# instance presents a single UDP port to the world and there is no allow-rule
# to keep chasing when a home ISP rotates its address pool.
#
# --ssh-public re-opens TCP 22, restricted to --ssh-cidr (your current /32 by
# default), for the case where the tunnel itself is what needs debugging.
aws_open_ports() {
  local region="$1" name cidr
  name="$(aws_instance_name "$region")"

  if [[ "${SSH_PUBLIC:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
    cidr="$(ssh_cidr)"
    step "UDP $VPN_PORT open to the internet; SSH exposed to $cidr"
    aws_ "$region" lightsail put-instance-public-ports \
      --instance-name "$name" \
      --port-infos \
        "fromPort=$VPN_PORT,toPort=$VPN_PORT,protocol=UDP,cidrs=0.0.0.0/0,ipv6Cidrs=::/0" \
        "fromPort=22,toPort=22,protocol=TCP,cidrs=$cidr" \
      >/dev/null
  else
    step "UDP $VPN_PORT open to the internet; SSH reachable only over the tunnel ($VPN_SERVER_V4)"
    aws_ "$region" lightsail put-instance-public-ports \
      --instance-name "$name" \
      --port-infos \
        "fromPort=$VPN_PORT,toPort=$VPN_PORT,protocol=UDP,cidrs=0.0.0.0/0,ipv6Cidrs=::/0" \
      >/dev/null
  fi
}

aws_up() {
  local region="$1" dns_mode="$2" ipv6_only="${3:-0}"
  local name bundle skey ip
  name="$(aws_instance_name "$region")"
  skey="$(server_key aws "$region")"

  if aws_exists "$region"; then
    warn "instance $name already exists in $region (state: $(aws_state "$region"))"
  else
    if [[ "$ipv6_only" == "1" ]]; then
      bundle="$(aws_resolve_bundle "$region" "$AWS_BUNDLE_IPV6")"
      warn "IPv6-only bundle: unreachable from IPv4-only networks (some hotel wifi, some carriers)"
    else
      bundle="$(aws_resolve_bundle "$region" "$AWS_BUNDLE_IPV4")"
    fi
    step "bundle $bundle, blueprint $AWS_BLUEPRINT"

    local ud; ud="$(mktemp)"
    build_user_data aws "$region" "$dns_mode" > "$ud"

    local az
    az="$(aws_ "$region" lightsail get-regions --include-availability-zones \
      --query "regions[?name=='$region'].availabilityZones[0].zoneName | [0]" --output text)"

    log "launching $name in $region ($az)"
    aws_ "$region" lightsail create-instances \
      --instance-names "$name" \
      --availability-zone "$az" \
      --blueprint-id "$AWS_BLUEPRINT" \
      --bundle-id "$bundle" \
      --user-data "file://$ud" \
      --tags "key=project,value=create-your-own-vpn" "key=managed-by,value=vpn.sh" \
      >/dev/null || { rm -f "$ud"; die "create-instances failed in $region"; }
    rm -f "$ud"
  fi

  # Wait for the instance to reach 'running' and receive a public address.
  log "waiting for instance to boot"
  local tries=0
  until [[ "$(aws_state "$region")" == "running" ]]; do
    (( ++tries > 60 )) && { wait_end; die "instance did not reach 'running' within 5 minutes"; }
    wait_dot; sleep 5
  done
  wait_end

  ip="$(aws_public_ip "$region")"
  [[ -n "$ip" && "$ip" != "None" ]] || die "instance has no public IPv4 address"

  aws_open_ports "$region"

  state_set '.servers[$k].endpoint = $e | .servers[$k].instance = $n | .servers[$k].updated = $t' \
    --arg k "$skey" --arg e "$ip" --arg n "$name" --arg t "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"

  ok "$region is up at $ip"
}

aws_down() {
  local region="$1" name
  name="$(aws_instance_name "$region")"
  if ! aws_exists "$region"; then
    warn "no instance in $region — nothing to delete"
    return 0
  fi
  log "deleting $name in $region"
  aws_ "$region" lightsail delete-instance --instance-name "$name" >/dev/null \
    || die "delete-instance failed in $region"
  state_set '.servers[$k].endpoint = null | .servers[$k].instance = null | .servers[$k].updated = $t' \
    --arg k "$(server_key aws "$region")" --arg t "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  ok "$region deleted — billing for it has stopped"
}

# Lightsail hands out a short-lived SSH key on demand, so the tool never has to
# create, store, or rotate a key pair of its own.
aws_ssh() {
  local region="$1"; shift
  local name tmp ip user rc=0
  name="$(aws_instance_name "$region")"
  tmp="$(mktemp -d)"
  # These are credentials on disk: remove them however this function exits,
  # including when ssh fails under `set -e`.
  trap 'rm -rf "$tmp"' RETURN

  # One call for everything: Lightsail hands out a short-lived key AND a signed
  # certificate, so the tool never creates or stores a key pair of its own.
  aws_ "$region" lightsail get-instance-access-details --instance-name "$name" \
    --output json > "$tmp/access.json" 2>/dev/null \
    || die "could not get access details for $name"

  jq -r '.accessDetails.privateKey' "$tmp/access.json" > "$tmp/key"
  chmod 600 "$tmp/key"
  user="$(jq -r '.accessDetails.username' "$tmp/access.json")"

  # Lightsail authenticates with a certificate; without it sshd rejects the
  # key outright with "Permission denied (publickey)".
  local certopt=()
  if [[ "$(jq -r '.accessDetails.certKey // empty' "$tmp/access.json")" != "" ]]; then
    jq -r '.accessDetails.certKey' "$tmp/access.json" > "$tmp/key-cert.pub"
    chmod 600 "$tmp/key-cert.pub"
    certopt=(-o "CertificateFile=$tmp/key-cert.pub")
  fi

  if [[ "${SSH_PUBLIC:-0}" == "1" ]]; then
    ip="$(jq -r '.accessDetails.ipAddress' "$tmp/access.json")"
  else
    # SSH is not published to the internet; reach it across the VPN.
    ip="$VPN_SERVER_V4"
  fi

  ssh -i "$tmp/key" "${certopt[@]}" \
      -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o UserKnownHostsFile=/dev/null \
      -o LogLevel=ERROR -o ConnectTimeout=15 "$user@$ip" "$@" || rc=$?
  if [[ $rc -ne 0 && "${SSH_PUBLIC:-0}" != "1" ]]; then
    warn "SSH is reachable only over the tunnel ($VPN_SERVER_V4) — connect the VPN first,"
    warn "or relaunch with --ssh-public to expose port 22 to your own address."
  fi
  return $rc
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# common.sh — shared helpers: logging, state, key generation, config rendering.
# Sourced by vpn.sh and the provider libraries. Not executable on its own.

# ---------------------------------------------------------------- constants --

VPN_NET_V4="${VPN_NET_V4:-10.66.66.0/24}"
VPN_NET_V6="${VPN_NET_V6:-fd66:66:66::/64}"
VPN_SERVER_V4="${VPN_SERVER_V4:-10.66.66.1}"
VPN_SERVER_V6="${VPN_SERVER_V6:-fd66:66:66::1}"
VPN_PORT="${VPN_PORT:-51820}"
VPN_MTU="${VPN_MTU:-1420}"
VPN_KEEPALIVE="${VPN_KEEPALIVE:-25}"

STATE_DIR="${VPN_STATE_DIR:-$ROOT_DIR/.vpn}"
STATE_FILE="$STATE_DIR/state.json"
CLIENT_DIR="$STATE_DIR/clients"

# ------------------------------------------------------------------ logging --

if [[ -t 2 && -z "${NO_COLOR:-}" ]]; then
  C_RST=$'\033[0m'; C_DIM=$'\033[2m'; C_RED=$'\033[31m'
  C_GRN=$'\033[32m'; C_YEL=$'\033[33m'; C_BLU=$'\033[34m'
else
  C_RST=''; C_DIM=''; C_RED=''; C_GRN=''; C_YEL=''; C_BLU=''
fi

log()   { printf '%s==>%s %s\n' "$C_BLU" "$C_RST" "$*" >&2; }
ok()    { printf '%s  ✓%s %s\n' "$C_GRN" "$C_RST" "$*" >&2; }
warn()  { printf '%s  !%s %s\n' "$C_YEL" "$C_RST" "$*" >&2; }
step()  { printf '%s  ·%s %s\n' "$C_DIM" "$C_RST" "$*" >&2; }
die()   { printf '%serror:%s %s\n' "$C_RED" "$C_RST" "$*" >&2; exit 1; }

# Spinner-free progress for long waits; prints a dot every poll.
wait_dot() { printf '.' >&2; }
wait_end() { printf '\n' >&2; }

# ------------------------------------------------------------ prerequisites --

need_cmd() {
  command -v "$1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "'$1' not found. $2"
}

check_base_deps() {
  need_cmd openssl "Install it: https://openssl.org (macOS: brew install openssl)"
  need_cmd jq      "Install it: https://jqlang.github.io/jq (macOS: brew install jq)"
  # openssl must support X25519 for key generation.
  openssl genpkey -algorithm X25519 -out /dev/null 2>/dev/null \
    || die "your openssl lacks X25519 support (need OpenSSL 1.1.1+). macOS: brew install openssl"
}

# -------------------------------------------------------------- key material --

# WireGuard keys are raw 32-byte X25519 values, base64-encoded. OpenSSL can
# produce them without the wireguard-tools package being installed locally:
# take the last 32 bytes of the DER encoding, which is the raw scalar / point.
wg_genkey() {
  openssl genpkey -algorithm X25519 2>/dev/null | openssl pkey -outform DER 2>/dev/null \
    | tail -c 32 | base64 | tr -d '\n'
}

wg_pubkey() {
  # $1 = base64 private key. Rebuild a DER private key and extract the public.
  local der_prefix='MC4CAQAwBQYDK2VuBCIEIA=='
  { printf '%s' "$der_prefix" | base64 -d; printf '%s' "$1" | base64 -d; } \
    | openssl pkey -inform DER -pubout -outform DER 2>/dev/null \
    | tail -c 32 | base64 | tr -d '\n'
}

wg_genpsk() { openssl rand -base64 32 | tr -d '\n'; }

# --------------------------------------------------------------------- state --

state_init() {
  mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" "$CLIENT_DIR"
  chmod 700 "$STATE_DIR"
  [[ -f "$STATE_FILE" ]] || echo '{"version":1,"clients":{},"servers":{}}' > "$STATE_FILE"
  chmod 600 "$STATE_FILE"
}

state_get() { jq -r "$1" "$STATE_FILE"; }

# Atomic read-modify-write so an interrupted run cannot truncate the state.
state_set() {
  local filter="$1"; shift
  local tmp; tmp="$(mktemp "$STATE_DIR/.state.XXXXXX")"
  jq "$@" "$filter" "$STATE_FILE" > "$tmp" || { rm -f "$tmp"; die "state update failed"; }
  mv "$tmp" "$STATE_FILE"
  chmod 600 "$STATE_FILE"
}

server_key() { printf '%s/%s' "$1" "$2"; }   # provider/region

# ------------------------------------------------------------------- clients --

# Assign the lowest free host address in the tunnel subnet, starting at .2
# (.1 is the server). Reuses an existing assignment if the client is known.
client_next_ip() {
  # Pin IFS locally so word splitting here cannot be broken by a caller.
  local used i
  local IFS=$' \t\n'
  used="$(state_get '[.clients[].ipv4] | join(" ")')"
  for i in $(seq 2 254); do
    [[ " $used " == *" 10.66.66.$i "* ]] || { echo "10.66.66.$i"; return; }
  done
  die "tunnel subnet exhausted (254 clients)"
}

client_ensure() {
  local name="$1" priv pub ip idx
  if [[ "$(state_get ".clients[\"$name\"] // empty")" != "" ]]; then
    return 0
  fi
  priv="$(wg_genkey)"; pub="$(wg_pubkey "$priv")"; ip="$(client_next_ip)"
  idx="${ip##*.}"
  state_set '.clients[$n] = {priv:$p, pub:$u, ipv4:$i, ipv6:$s, created:$t}' \
    --arg n "$name" --arg p "$priv" --arg u "$pub" --arg i "$ip" \
    --arg s "fd66:66:66::$idx" --arg t "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  ok "created client key: $name ($ip)"
}

# ------------------------------------------------------------ config render --

resolve_dns() {
  case "${1:-cloudflare}" in
    cloudflare) echo "1.1.1.2, 1.0.0.2" ;;          # malware-blocking resolver
    quad9)      echo "9.9.9.9, 149.112.112.112" ;;
    google)     echo "8.8.8.8, 8.8.4.4" ;;
    unbound|adguard) echo "$VPN_SERVER_V4" ;;        # resolver runs on the server
    *)          echo "$1" ;;                          # caller passed literal IPs
  esac
}

# render_client_config <client> <provider> <region>
render_client_config() {
  local name="$1" prov="$2" region="$3" skey
  skey="$(server_key "$prov" "$region")"
  local cpriv cipv4 cipv6 spub psk endpoint port dns
  cpriv="$(state_get ".clients[\"$name\"].priv")"
  cipv4="$(state_get ".clients[\"$name\"].ipv4")"
  cipv6="$(state_get ".clients[\"$name\"].ipv6")"
  spub="$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"].pub")"
  psk="$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"].psk[\"$name\"] // empty")"
  endpoint="$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"].endpoint")"
  port="$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"].port")"
  dns="$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"].dns")"

  cat <<EOF
[Interface]
PrivateKey = $cpriv
Address = $cipv4/32, $cipv6/128
DNS = $dns
MTU = $VPN_MTU

[Peer]
PublicKey = $spub
$([[ -n "$psk" ]] && echo "PresharedKey = $psk")
Endpoint = $endpoint:$port
AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0, ::/0
PersistentKeepalive = $VPN_KEEPALIVE
EOF
}

# Write every known client's config for one server, plus a QR code if possible.
emit_configs() {
  local prov="$1" region="$2" name outdir f
  outdir="$CLIENT_DIR/$prov-$region"
  mkdir -p "$outdir"; chmod 700 "$outdir"
  while IFS= read -r name; do
    [[ -z "$name" ]] && continue
    f="$outdir/$name.conf"
    render_client_config "$name" "$prov" "$region" > "$f"
    chmod 600 "$f"
    ok "config: ${f#$ROOT_DIR/}"
  done < <(state_get '.clients | keys[]')
}

show_qr() {
  local file="$1"
  if command -v qrencode >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    qrencode -t ansiutf8 < "$file"
  else
    warn "qrencode not installed — cannot print QR. Install: brew install qrencode"
    warn "Or import the file directly into the WireGuard app."
  fi
}

# --------------------------------------------------------------- user-data --

# Build the bootstrap script for a server: read cloudinit/bootstrap.sh and
# substitute the placeholders. Kept dependency-free (no envsubst).
#
# The payload is a shell script, not a #cloud-config document, because Lightsail
# routes user-data to cloud-init's script handler -- a YAML payload there is
# executed line by line by dash and silently does nothing.
#
# The peer list is injected separately from the scalar values: awk -v cannot
# carry a multi-line value, and the block sits inside a YAML block scalar, so
# every line has to be re-indented to match the placeholder's own indentation.
build_user_data() {
  # All locals are declared once here: bash 3.2 (still the default on macOS)
  # echoes a local that is re-declared inside a loop.
  local prov="$1" region="$2" dns_mode="$3" skey priv peers_file
  local name cpub cip cip6 psk
  skey="$(server_key "$prov" "$region")"
  priv="$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"].priv")"
  [[ -n "$priv" && "$priv" != "null" ]] || die "no server key for $skey"

  peers_file="$(mktemp)"
  while IFS= read -r name; do
    [[ -z "$name" ]] && continue
    cpub="$(state_get ".clients[\"$name\"].pub")"
    cip="$(state_get ".clients[\"$name\"].ipv4")"
    cip6="$(state_get ".clients[\"$name\"].ipv6")"
    psk="$(state_get ".servers[\"$skey\"].psk[\"$name\"] // empty")"
    {
      echo "# client: $name"
      echo "[Peer]"
      echo "PublicKey = $cpub"
      [[ -n "$psk" ]] && echo "PresharedKey = $psk"
      echo "AllowedIPs = $cip/32, $cip6/128"
      echo
    } >> "$peers_file"
  done < <(state_get '.clients | keys[]')

  [[ -s "$peers_file" ]] || { rm -f "$peers_file"; die "no clients defined — run: ./vpn.sh client add <name>"; }

  # Base64 keys only ever contain [A-Za-z0-9+/=], so '|' is a safe sed
  # delimiter and no replacement-side escaping is needed.
  sed -e "s|__SERVER_PRIVKEY__|$priv|g" \
      -e "s|__PORT__|$VPN_PORT|g" \
      -e "s|__MTU__|$VPN_MTU|g" \
      -e "s|__SERVER_V4__|$VPN_SERVER_V4|g" \
      -e "s|__SERVER_V6__|$VPN_SERVER_V6|g" \
      -e "s|__NET_V4__|$VPN_NET_V4|g" \
      -e "s|__NET_V6__|$VPN_NET_V6|g" \
      -e "s|__DNS_MODE__|$dns_mode|g" \
      "$ROOT_DIR/cloudinit/bootstrap.sh" \
  | awk -v pf="$peers_file" '
      /__PEERS__/ {
        match($0, /^[ \t]*/)
        indent = substr($0, 1, RLENGTH)
        while ((getline line < pf) > 0) print indent line
        close(pf)
        next
      }
      { print }
    '
  rm -f "$peers_file"
}

# ----------------------------------------------------------------- my public IP --

# The CIDR(s) allowed to reach SSH. Defaults to the caller's current address as
# a /32. --ssh-cidr accepts a comma-separated list, which is the right answer
# for a connection behind carrier-grade NAT: enumerate the handful of addresses
# the ISP actually uses and pin each one, rather than widening to a whole /24.
#
# `./vpn.sh pool` prints that list by sampling your egress address repeatedly.
ssh_cidr() {
  if [[ -n "${SSH_CIDR:-}" ]]; then
    echo "$SSH_CIDR"
  else
    echo "$(my_ip)/32"
  fi
}

# Sample the public address this machine exits from, repeatedly, and print each
# distinct one as a /32. Connections behind CGNAT rotate between several.
egress_pool() {
  local n="${1:-40}" i
  for ((i=0; i<n; i++)); do
    curl -fsS --max-time 5 https://checkip.amazonaws.com 2>/dev/null
  done | tr -d "\r" | sort -u | sed "s|$|/32|" | paste -sd, -
}

my_ip() {
  local ip
  ip="$(curl -fsS --max-time 8 https://checkip.amazonaws.com 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')" || true
  [[ -z "$ip" ]] && ip="$(curl -fsS --max-time 8 https://api.ipify.org 2>/dev/null | tr -d '[:space:]')" || true
  [[ -n "$ip" ]] || die "could not determine your public IP (needed to lock down SSH)"
  echo "$ip"
}
